item.title: Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe GOMBE — The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has disclosed that 98 persons were killed while 1,345 others sustained injuries in road traffic crashes recorded across Gombe State between January and September 2026. The FRSC Sector Commander in the state, Commander Samson Kaura, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing members of the Gombe State Council of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) during the commemoration of the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. Kaura said the command recorded 1,345 road traffic incidents during the nine-month period, adding that fatalities increased by six per cent compared with the corresponding period. He identified excessive speeding and reckless driving as major causes of road crashes and fatalities, warning that irresponsible road use continued to pose a serious threat to motorists and other road users. According to him, the annual World Day of Remembrance provides an opportunity to honour those who have lost their lives or sustained serious injuries in road crashes, while drawing attention to the need for stronger legal responses to traffic offences resulting in deaths and injuries. He said the commemoration also seeks to promote better support for crash victims and their families, as well as evidence-based interventions to prevent and ultimately eliminate road traffic deaths and injuries. The sector commander expressed concern that the fatalities recorded in the first nine months of 2026 had surpassed the figure for the whole of 2025. He said the command recorded 1,614 road traffic incidents in 2025, resulting in 92 deaths and 926 injuries. Kaura described the 2026 World Day of Remembrance as a campaign aimed at translating remembrance into concrete action, stressing the need for collective responsibility in addressing road traffic crashes. In his response, the Vice Chairman of the Gombe State NUJ Council, Emmanuel Akila, who represented the state chairman, Faruk Muazu Gombe, pledged the union’s continued cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety and development. Akila, however, urged the FRSC to strengthen collaboration with the union to identify and curb the activities of fake journalists in the state. He called on the corps to insist on proper identification of journalists during official engagements and other road-related activities to prevent impersonation and protect the integrity of the journalism profession. The NUJ vice chairman also urged the FRSC to intensify enforcement against vehicle overloading, describing the practice as one of the factors contributing to fatalities in road crashes. He stressed the need for sustained public enlightenment, effective enforcement of traffic regulations and stronger collaboration among relevant stakeholders to reduce road crashes and safeguard lives on the highways. item.title: UK, Nigeria seal $750m infrastructure deal as Pension funds prepare to unlock billions
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria and the United Kingdom have strengthened their economic partnership with a proposed $750 million infrastructure investment fund aimed at mobilising billions of dollars in pension assets to finance critical development projects across Nigeria and other selected African markets. The initiative, which has already attracted interest from 19 Nigerian pension funds, is expected to channel long-term domestic and international investments into key sectors, including energy, transportation and digital infrastructure, as both countries seek to address the continent’s widening infrastructure financing gap. A statement from PenCom disclosed that the agreement was signed by Nigeria’s Pension Industry Leadership Council, PILC,and UK-funded specialist development agency, FSD Africa, in Lagos on November 10, 2026. Under the agreement, FSD Africa will provide technical expertise and advisory support to PILC towards establishing the proposed investment platform, including the selection of a fund manager through a competitive process, engagement with prospective investors and development finance institutions, capacity building and support for necessary regulatory reforms. The initiative was developed by Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators, PFAs, with support from the National Pension Commission, PenCom, and FSD Africa. Speaking on the development, UK Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, said the partnership reflected the shared commitment of both countries to mobilising domestic capital, particularly pension funds, for productive investment in the real economy. According to him: “The UK is proud to partner with the Nigeria’s Pension Industry and the pensions regulator Pencom to progress this investment. Both our countries are prioritising tacking the challenge of attracting more domestic capital, including from pension funds, into the real economy. It is great to see Nigeria making concrete progress on its efforts and be a part of those opportunities to turn this ambition into investment, jobs, and economic growth.” On her part, Chair of the Nigeria Pension Industry Leadership Council and Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Ms Omolola Oloworaran, described the proposed investment platform as timely, stressing that the pension industry was committed to deploying its substantial pool of long-term savings towards national development while protecting contributors’ retirement funds. She said: “The pension industry holds the largest pool of long-term savings capital in the country, and we are committed to mobilising it to deepen infrastructure development, while safeguarding the retirement savings of contributors. item.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The hearing will be streamed live on YouTube. This will be Smith’s 14th congressional hearing exclusively on Nigeria. In November 2025, he chaired a hearing after President Donald Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a ‘country of particular concern’. In May 2016, he also chaired a hearing on “The U.S. role in helping Nigeria confront Boko Haram and other threats in northern Nigeria.” The post US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Carrick set to be sacked by Man Utd: reports
item.description: Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side’s dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday. United’s hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club’s miserable form and it is believed that Carrick will shortly be relieved of his duties. United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United owners the Glazer family and influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe would then decide whether to act on that recommendation. Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old, hired on a permanent basis in the close season after a successful interim spell last term, had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. United’s surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively. They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But United’s powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle. USA boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to secure a replacement for Carrick before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. item.title: Wenger considers challenging Infantino for FIFA presidency — Report
item.description: Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering a challenge against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, according to the BBC. The 77-year-old Frenchman is giving serious thought to contesting the position following growing calls from influential figures in European football for him to enter the race. Some of Wenger’s supporters have reportedly indicated that they would back him even if he chose to step down before completing the four-year presidential term. His possible candidacy could pose a significant challenge to Infantino, whose leadership has faced criticism following the collapse of a plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Although the controversy has unsettled his position in parts of European football, Infantino retains considerable support in South America, Africa and Asia. He recently maintained that he enjoys the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of the global football community. Wenger, who currently serves as Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development, is expected to enjoy the backing of the Union of European Football Associations (Uefa), which has led opposition to Infantino over the abandoned commercial proposal. However, sources close to the Frenchman told BBC Sport that he has yet to make a final decision on whether to contest the election. They also believe Infantino remains the favourite to secure another term. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to challenge Infantino is November 18, ahead of the election scheduled for March. Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega became the first candidate to announce his intention to run in October, while Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also indicated interest in the position. item.title: Why I rejected US asylum offer before Abacha arrested me — Obasanjo
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has revealed that he rejected an offer of political asylum from the United States despite being warned that he would be arrested if he returned to Nigeria under the late military Head of State, Gen. Sani Abacha. Obasanjo also recounted how he ventured into farming after retiring from the Nigerian Army at 42. The former president disclosed this while narrating his experience under the military government in an interview published by BBC News Pidgin on Tuesday. He said, “When I was leaving government as military head of state, I was leaving too early. I didn’t join the army to retire at the age of 42. “Now I had to retire at the age of 42. At the age of 42, I had become a four-star general. There’s nothing else I can do in the army. I’ve become the military head of state. That’s the highest political office I could rise. Obasanjo said his farming business was progressing well until Abacha’s government moved against him. He said he rejected the US asylum because he had committed no crime. “So what can I do? I decided I would go into farming. It really was going well, and it went well until I was arrested. “Abacha had decided that I must be liquidated; otherwise he would not be able to have his way. I didn’t know that. I was travelling and coming back, and the American ambassador in Nigeria called me and said his country had offered me political asylum because they knew that I would be arrested if I returned home. “This was difficult for me. I don’t— I haven’t done anything. What do they want to arrest me for? Um, I don’t want political asylum.” He said his passport was later seized, after which he proceeded to his farm. On arrival, one of his security personnel informed him that government security operatives had surrounded the premises. According to him, a police officer dressed in civilian clothes subsequently approached him, claiming that an Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) had invited him. “And when I arrived, they seized my passport; I made for my farm. At the gate of my farm was my security. He waved me down. He said that security had surrounded the farm. And within 15 minutes, this man came in mufti, not in uniform, a policeman, and he said, ‘Well, you have been invited by the AIG to come and help him.’ I said, ‘You are a fool.’ “‘If the AIG wants me to help him, he will not be inviting me. He will come here,” Obasanjo lamented, adding, “So it was my own car that I used to take myself to the police station. We saw the AIG, and the AIG said, ‘I have been instructed to arrest you.’” The former president also disclosed that former United States President Jimmy Carter intervened on his behalf by appealing to Abacha. item.title: US Judge Orders Psychiatric Exam For Meghan Markle’s Father
item.description: A US judge has ordered a psychiatric examination for Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Prince Harry’s wife, Meghan Markle, after his arrest for alleged possession of images of child sexual abuse. Thomas Markle, 82, is charged with one count of “possession of child pornography” and made an initial court appearance in Tampa in Florida on Friday. Judge Lindsay Griffin cited his “health condition,” “advanced age” and “lack of recall” in the order issued on Friday, without providing further details. Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents earlier that day at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida. The Justice Department said he allegedly “kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades.” File photo of Meghan and Thomas Markle Pictures of child sex abuse have also allegedly been found at Markle’s former home in the Philippines and at a storage unit he rented in Mexico. The judge said she found “reasonable cause to believe” that Markle was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense.” She instructed a psychiatrist to provide a report on Markle’s mental state by November 20. The judge permitted Markle to be moved to house arrest with electronic monitoring, CNN reported. Markle had been living in Cebu in the Philippines until reportedly returning to the United States this year. Meghan Markle said last month that she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse. He could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. item.title: ‘I didn’t tell them to go buy votes,’ Wike defends N10m reward for councillors
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said he never asked councillors to buy votes with the N10 million he promised those who deliver their wards in the 2027 general elections. “I didn’t tell them, ‘Take this money and go and buy votes.’ I said, ‘Go and work. Show commitment. Demonstrate that you really mean what you are talking about. When you win, come, and we are going to reward you,” he said. Wike spoke on Tuesday during an inspection of ongoing infrastructure projects in Abuja. He was responding to criticism of the promise, which he said was an incentive for hard work and not an attempt to buy votes. Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali Area Council the previous day, Wike had explained that the initiative was part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level. “For the councillors, you have a task. I will hold a meeting with you again, and I will now say the way I am going to mobilise you, but I will give you a bet, like what is happening in the stars; it’s a competition. “Anybody who delivers his ward, if you deliver your ward, that is what the Rainbow Coalition has decided to do as mobilisation and support for Mr President; we have to start in the FCT (I couldn’t say so when the president came because they gave me only two minutes to talk). But now that I have time to talk, let me say that the Rainbow Coalition all over the federation, as a form of mobilisation for Mr President to win this election, is saying that any councillor that delivers his ward will come and take N10 million. We want to mobilise for Mr President. So, go to your wards, and go and see your leaders. I know only you cannot do it, but we are using you as an instrumentality for your leaders. Go and meet your leaders and say, ‘Look, oh, there is something that has come.’ We must not allow this thing to go. Let’s dedicate our ward for Mr President’. So, that is for that,” Wike had said. Speaking on Tuesday, Wike drew a line between rewarding political commitment and offering money to voters in exchange for their support. He said the councillors were challenged to prove their commitment through effective mobilisation. To make his case, he pointed to athletes who are promised houses or other benefits if they return from international competitions with trophies. He asked why a similar reward in politics should automatically be read as bribery. He also faulted sections of the media for failing to tell legitimate rewards apart from vote-buying. Political parties and candidates, he argued, routinely spend money on campaign advertisements without facing the same scrutiny. Wike urged journalists to pay closer attention to the difference between financial inducements meant to sway voters and rewards promised to political mobilisers for hitting set targets. item.title: French Students Block Dozens Of Schools
item.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality. The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year. With the European Union’s second biggest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Students dance in front of police officers during a rally over learning conditions as part of a nationwide day of action, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Paris on November 5, 2026. Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15- to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon. “Now is the time to step up the mobilisation by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday. Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure. “We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said. The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools. But students say this is not enough. Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs”. They have called for a new day of strikes and protests on November 17. Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million. item.title: CAF reschedules 2026 Awards ceremony to December 2 in Lagos
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has rescheduled the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony to December 2 in Lagos. CAF announced the new date in a statement on Tuesday, with the event brought forward five days. Although the football body gave no reason for the change, the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Art Theatre, in Lagos, remains the venue for the ceremony. The event will mark the return of the CAF Awards to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition, bringing together leading players, coaches, clubs and other personalities in African football to celebrate their achievements. A total of 18 categories will be recognised at the ceremony, with the CAF Men’s Player of the Year and CAF Women’s Player of the Year awards among the major honours. Other categories will recognise outstanding coaches, goalkeepers, emerging talents, clubs and national teams for their performances during the year. Meanwhile, voting for the 2026 awards is ongoing and will run from November 5 to 20 across the men’s and women’s categories. item.title: Iran calls on US to meet its demands to end war
item.description: Iran on Tuesday urged the United States to meet its demands in a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after President Donald Trump spoke of “positive momentum” to end their eight-month war. “The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran’s IRNA news agency. “The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.” Tehran has proposed reopening Hormuz, which it has blockaded since the start of the war, within two days in return for Washington meeting a raft of conditions. These include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Trump, whose Republican party last week lost midterm elections in part due to the war, said on Monday that there was “positive momentum” towards ending the conflict after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House. In a post on social media, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded” but said further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”. “We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said. Diplomatic efforts, led by Qatar and Pakistan, are underway to find a resolution to the war, which broke out in late February when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. On Tuesday, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to “surrender” to the Iranian demands. “The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks,” said Rezaei, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in a post on X. item.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
item.description: …As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024. Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August. The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent. The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line. The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August. Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August. Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent. However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August. Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none. The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter. Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators. item.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot seeks government
item.description: Israel’s new parliament will be sworn in Tuesday, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority even as rival Gadi Eisenkot still works to form a new government. President Isaac Herzog will deliver a speech at 4:00 pm (1400 GMT) for the swearing-in of the 120-seat parliament, in which neither Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc nor Eisenkot’s opposition will hold a majority. The opposition hopes to use its newfound legislative power to move quickly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas, the deadliest day in Israel’s history. Herzog on Sunday gave Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to cobble together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Ahead of the parliament opening, Eisenkot’s party announced progress in naming people to seek key positions. The opposition will put forward Matan Kahana — like Eisenkot a former senior military figure — as speaker of the parliament, Eisenkot’s Yashar party said. Avigdor Lieberman, a right-wing opposition leader who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee. The opposition’s choice for speaker would need to secure a larger number of votes than anyone backed by Netanyahu’s bloc, which has been trying to push back a vote on the speaker. The newly formed government would need 61 votes to be approved to take office. Eisenkot could secure the threshold with support from Arab-Israeli lawmakers, who secured a record number of seats on the back of anger in the minority community over Netanyahu’s hard-right government. But Lieberman had been clear he would not allow Eisenkot to rely on Arab-Israelis to come to power. He has instead proposed an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, despite his years of bitter denunciations of the community for its singular priority on maintaining an exemption from mandatory military service. Eisenkot’s core opposition bloc has fewer seats than Netanyahu at 48, but would achieve a majority if the 19 Arab-Israeli lawmakers either enter the government or, more likely, vote for it without joining. The two ultra-Orthodox parties, with 13 seats, could also crown Eisenkot if they ditch their long alliance with Netanyahu, who backed the exemption from military service without enshrining it fully into law. An alliance with either group would likely be fragile. Arab-Israelis are likely to object if Eisenkot carries out another major offensive in Gaza. Eisenkot has largely backed Netanyahu’s war decisions, although he has vowed to crack down on extremist settlers in the West Bank who have been attacking and stealing from Palestinians with virtual impunity. item.title: Obasanjo betrayed Babangida over one-term power-sharing agreement — Kalu alleges
item.description: ***Discloses why his relationship with Obasanjo collapsed, promises to groom younger Nigerians for leadership ***Recalls financing PDP’s formation, how party members turned against him By Henry Umoru, Abuja Chairman Senate Committee on South East Development Commission (SEDC), Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, APC, Abia North, has revealed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo betrayed his agreement to serve one term and to subsequently hand over to the North. Kalu has, however, revealed an account of an alleged political understanding involving Obasanjo and former military president Ibrahim Babangida ahead of the 2003 presidential election. The former Abia State governor, who spoke on why his once cordial relationship with Obasanjo eventually collapsed, disclosed that their disagreement was rooted partly in what he described as an agreement that Obasanjo would serve only one four-year term before power returned to the North. According to him, the understanding was reached during a meeting involving himself, Obasanjo and Babangida at Obasanjo’s residence in Ota, Ogun State, stressing that the arrangement was intended to accommodate the political circumstances surrounding the emergence of Obasanjo in 1999, following the annulment of the June 12, 1993, presidential election. The former Senate Whip spoke on Monday night during an exclusive appearance on Arise PrimeTime, the flagship evening current affairs programme of Arise News Television, anchored by Charles Aniagolu. Kalu maintained that the agreement was for Obasanjo to complete one term and hand over to another political leader from the North, allowing the country’s power rotation arrangement to continue. When asked specifically to speak about reports that Babangida was expected to succeed Obasanjo in 2003, with Kalu potentially becoming his running mate, the senator said he could not confirm the vice-presidential arrangement but stood by the agreement concerning Obasanjo’s tenure. “Well, I cannot be certain about the vice presidency, but I can tell you, yes, this was our discussion in Ota. That he would leave, he would leave for four years and give back to the North,” he disclosed. Providing further details, Kalu identified an individual he described as Obasanjo’s aide from Benue State, named Adobeye in the interview, as being present during the discussion. He said, “What we discussed and agreed there were people there, there were people there, like His Boy, Obasanjo’s Boy, Adobeye from Benue State; he was sitting down there where we sat, me, Ibrahim Babangida and President Obasanjo. Where we agreed, we agreed.” Kalu said the disagreement over the alleged arrangement was among the issues that eventually damaged his relationship with the former president, just as he accused Obasanjo of using state institutions, particularly the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), to pursue political opponents and remove elected governors through what he considered unconstitutional means. item.title: Rwandan author urges readers to turn knowledge into wisdom
item.description: Rwandan author, entrepreneur and cultural advocate, Lisa Munezero, has said self-awareness, resilience, discipline and purposeful action can influence the direction of people’s lives, saying individuals must look beyond conventional definitions of success. Munezero also warned that qualifications, ambition and access to opportunities alone do not guarantee fulfilment. The author stated this in the book: ‘The Well of Knowing: 8 Lessons of Becoming,’ set to be unveiled at a public presentation on November 14, 2026, at 1:00 p.m., at Four Points by Sheraton, Victoria Island, Lagos, Nigeria. Attendance is by invitation. The publication introduces eight interconnected lessons exploring the relationship between knowledge, personal development, purposeful living and the decisions that shape individual achievement. Its central proposition is that what people do with what they know shapes the opportunities they create and the people they become. Drawing on entrepreneurial experiences, personal reflections and practical wisdom, Munezero invites readers to look beyond conventional definitions of success and consider how self-awareness, resilience, discipline and purposeful action can influence the direction of their lives. The Well of Knowing asks how individuals discover purpose, learn from rejection and failure, turn ideas into opportunities, and transform acquired knowledge into wisdom, influence and lasting contributions to society. Addressing students, aspiring entrepreneurs, professionals and emerging leaders, the book presents personal development as an ongoing journey. It also explores mentorship, relationships and responsible leadership as ways in which individual growth can benefit communities and future generations. In his foreword, teacher, poet, dramatist and founder of Step Out Creatives Publications in the United Kingdom, Dr Isi Agboaye, highlights the book’s emphasis on purpose and action and draws a comparison with Norman Vincent Peale’s The Power of Positive Thinking. Senior banking professional and author of Threads of Love and Duty, Aderonke Adeyinka, recommends the publication to aspiring entrepreneurs and readers interested in personal growth, recognizing its attention to resilience and lifelong learning. Kenyan literary journalist, blogger and podcaster, James Murua, commends its treatment of mentorship, community relationships and intergenerational knowledge-sharing. item.title: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
item.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump’s — apparently jovial — offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post — but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was “only kidding.” The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room. “So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?” Trump said. “Thank you for the offer, sir — for the offer, I have no, no — I do not want to be in politics,” White replied. Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody.” The press secretary’s post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job. Trump’s announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to “violent Fighter and Warrior” White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party’s stunning midterm elections defeat. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year. But there was also some skepticism about the president’s announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking. – ‘Beat the hell out of you’ – Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been “having a little fun.” “He’s a great guy,” Trump told the room full of reporters. “The only problem is he’ll talk for a little while and then he’s going to beat the hell out of you.” Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon — the ring used for UFC fights. “I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” he joked — before quickliy adding: “I have zero political aspirations.” White added that “the last 24 hours of my life has been insane” since Trump made the announcement. Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything… I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.” Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. item.title: N10m reward to motivate FCT councillors, not vote buying — APC chair defends Wike
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Nentawe Yilwatda, has defended the N10 million reward promised by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to councillors who deliver their wards for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, on Monday, Yilwatda said the money was intended to motivate councillors and would be paid after the election, once the result had been established. “He was speaking to the FCT councillors in the forum, and I’m sure it’s addressing something about 62 or 60-something councillors in the FCT,” he said. Asked whether the offer amounted to voter inducement, Yilwatda rejected the suggestion, arguing that political parties routinely provide funds for mobilisation. “Which political party doesn’t release money for mobilisation? Which political party? So, tell me one. No, it’s not for votes. The same reward for you to deliver Tinubu in your ward,” he said. Yilwatda compared the offer to rewarding students for academic achievement but maintained that the timing of the payment was significant. “The money is not given before the election. It doesn’t matter? No, it matters. It matters because if the money is given after the election has been concluded and the winner has been declared and there’s nothing at stake again—if the court has proven and all the legal rules have been followed—that you legally deliver your ward by giving you N10 million,” he said. Asked again whether he considered the offer of vote buying, Yilwatda replied authoritatively: “Never.” Wike made the pledge at a political meeting in Kwali Area Council, promising N10 million to each councillor who delivers their ward for Tinubu and the APC in 2027. Asked whether the APC would return Godswill Akpabio as Senate President if he wins re-election, Yilwatda said the decision would rest with senators. “Let’s wait for the election first. I don’t have anybody in mind. The Senate will determine who they want to make the Senate President,” he said. On reports of electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, Yilwatda said he sympathised with anyone injured and said the APC supported free and fair elections. “If anybody is injured by anybody across the country, I’m sure it shouldn’t be by APC supporters. I pity anybody who is being injured, and I sympathise with them. Our party stands for free and fair elections,” he said. item.title: Trump sees ‘positive momentum’ on Iran after Qatar PM talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was momentum toward ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country “militarily, is effectively over,” but kept open the possibility of new strikes. Trump met at the White House with Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani — a key mediator in the Iran war. It was his first meeting with a foreign leader since his party’s massive losses in the midterm elections. Trump later posted on Truth Social that the two leaders had “an excellent conversation” and that “much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran.” In the weeks leading up to the midterms, there was widespread speculation that US strikes against Iran would resume soon after. However, Trump has talked down resuming the conflict while leaving the door open to further strikes — a position he reiterated Monday at a White House press briefing. “Iran, militarily, is effectively over. We’re just keeping it the status quo,” Trump told reporters. “But if we do have to go back in, we are locked and loaded, and ready to go.” In his social post on Monday, Trump said that he believed further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo.” “We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said. – ‘Imaginary talks’ – Iranian officials meanwhile expressed defiance at the continued pressure from Washington. The Islamic republic’s top security chief, Mohsen Rezai, wrote on X late Monday that the US “flails like a desperate gambler,” telling Washington to “fold your hand. Stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks.” Earlier, Tehran’s top negotiator Mahammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed on X that Israel was pushing the US deeper into conflict, adding that “unless Washington drops the ‘Israel First’ mindset, America and its allies are headed straight for a dark age.” On the ground in Iran, strikes — which have not been publicly acknowledged by the US military — are continuing, according to Iranian authorities. The island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, was targeted overnight from Sunday to Monday, the provincial deputy governor stated on state television. Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat, not least because it has contributed to rising prices in the US economy. item.title: I give kudos to people who sent me to jail; it’s like school – Orji Kalu
item.description: Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has praised those responsible for his imprisonment, saying the six months he spent behind bars gave him valuable life lessons and made him a more humble person. Kalu said rather than regret his incarceration, he considers it an experience that changed his understanding of life and helped him develop a different outlook. The former Abia State governor made the remarks during an interview on Arise Television on Monday. Explaining why he was grateful for the experience, Kalu said, “It made me more humble. It made me to realise that life is not the same thing I used to think about. So I’m very grateful to God I was there.” He added, “And I gave kudos to people that sent me there because it’s like going to school. And I graduated there, and I’m very happy I went there.” Kalu was convicted by a Federal High Court in Lagos in December 2019 on a 39-count charge and sentenced to 12 years’ imprisonment. However, the Supreme Court overturned the conviction on May 8, 2020, ruling that the trial judge, Mohammed Idris, lacked jurisdiction to deliver the judgment after his elevation to the Court of Appeal. The apex court ordered a fresh trial, and Kalu was released from Kuje Correctional Centre after spending approximately six months in custody. Asked whether he believed the conviction was justified, the senator disagreed but said he did not wish to dwell on the matter. “No, it wasn’t the right thing to do. But I don’t like to discuss this because the judge had his reasons. When the judge did it, I praised him. I support all his decisions,” he said. Kalu also acknowledged that the judiciary had its challenges but maintained that some judges remained committed to dispensing justice. He advised Nigerians dissatisfied with rulings of lower courts to pursue appeals rather than publicly condemn judicial decisions. According to him, taking cases to higher courts gives litigants another opportunity to obtain justice, as more judges are involved in reviewing the decisions. item.title: Atiku congratulates Nigerian athletes on three Dakar Youth Olympic gold medals
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has congratulated Nigerian athletes following their historic performance at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, where Team Nigeria won three gold medals in athletics. Atiku, in a post on his X account on Tuesday, particularly celebrated Rosemary Nwankwo, Gift Bright and Praise Ugoh for their victories in the women’s 100 metres, men’s 100 metres and women’s 400 metres events, respectively. He described the athletes’ performance as historic, noting that Nwankwo and Bright won the women’s and men’s 100 metres titles on the same day, marking the first time Nigeria had recorded such a double at the Youth Olympic Games. He also congratulated Ugoh for winning the women’s 400 metres title in her first final over the distance at the competition, becoming the first Nigerian to claim the event’s gold medal at the Games. “These young Nigerians have shown the world what discipline, courage and self-belief can achieve. Their success is a reminder that our nation’s greatest wealth lies in her youth, and that when we invest in their talent, they will raise our flag on every stage,” Atiku said. The former vice-president pledged to continue advocating support for young Nigerians, particularly in providing facilities and opportunities for talented individuals to excel. He also congratulated the athletes’ coaches and families, describing their achievements as a source of pride for the country. item.title: China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria!
item.description: I came looking for ancient soldiers and left thinking about Nigeria’s tourism potential! One of the things I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures and, of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepares you for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! For anyone who has watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there! But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to around 221 BC, when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that! While some people prepare for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation! The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. And what makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over two thousand years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974, when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army! I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. UNESCO designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. But beyond the fascinating history, what struck me most was what China has done with this discovery. This is where the story becomes particularly interesting for Nigeria. China has not simply uncovered an ancient treasure and left it to gather dust. It has invested in archaeological research, conservation, restoration, museum infrastructure, visitor facilities and tourism development. The preservation work itself is remarkable.
